svg.text: Flywheel next — four tiers of one machinery: what runs, what wakes it, what it clones · git stays the one state store under all four

no tier above 0 is a new architecture — a tick is a pure function of fetched state (136, 217a), so a tier differs only in where the tick is invoked, what the process clones and who owns the bot · the wake path is an event reaching a stopped machine; the tick path is the same fetch → list → read → evaluate → effect everywhere
WAKE · the tick is invoked, not looped (244) — every invoker produces the same tick
acks inside three seconds · a retry buffer, not state (246)
the scheduler · always on, because the platform has no cron
it sweeps the due index (245) — one row per organization, the earliest time a tick could change anything — and starts the due tenants through the Machines API
PLATFORMS · Fly.io Machines vs Lambda microVMs — both Firecracker; the contract differs
Lambda sells a bounded invocation with no durable disk · Fly sells a microVM you create, stop and restart with a volume attached
a 900-second cap against sessions of hours (I5);
/tmp gone between environments, so 205's root cannot persist
the capture endpoint and Slack interactions
but it cannot hold the Discord gateway, so 216's
presenter job has no home there
the fit — from the tenant's image, one volume, no cap
the proxy wakes it; stopped, it is billed for rootfs only
the whole machinery on one machine · zero cost to serve
design and construction places, on disk
state and blueprints in full, and every
local — a pane or a daemon — or the
your machine, in its own worktrees
whatever you set up · your own bot and token
costs nothing and serves nobody but you
asleep when the laptop is asleep; the sink lease waits with the pin
one step above your own computer · cents per tenant per month
stopped when idle — no process, rootfs only on the bill
the state repository's shared line, and the
records, threads, responses, its sink lease,
its heartbeat, run records, the status page
a built repository, a place, a worktree
the platform's shared bot, interactions mode
controls and the numbered grammar; no secret placed (217d)
gives up plain typed messages while the machine sleeps
every decision is still answerable by control and number (155)
work on demand · the bill tracks usage, not tenancy
from the organization's image (239), through the platform's API
for one session or more · retired when idle (240)
hosts added while demand holds, within bound
and cost; retired as the queue drains (242)
retire destroys the machine — it never merely stops it
a stopped machine keeps its host id and stops heartbeating: stale at five minutes,
gone at thirty, raising a takeover decision for a host that is only parked
state, blueprints and the tracked built repositories
worktrees live here · the volume outlives the host as a cache (248)
the dispatcher stays tier 1's · a pool adds work, never a second dispatcher
your own container, bot and network · a machine plus your platform
the long-lived loop, one process per host id (231)
your own, on your own placement
your own pool, at whatever bound you set
your own app and token · the audit line names it
your tailnet node or your ingress · the endpoint yours
gives up nothing · costs a machine that runs whether or not anything happens
the only tier whose tick is a loop rather than an invocation
GIT HOST · the one state store, under every tier
an effect lands by compare-and-swap on a ref, and a repeat under the same key writes nothing (134, 111, I15) · every tier fetches here and pushes here, and holds nothing else as truth (I14)
object records · threads · responses · leases · decisions · heartbeats — one root per organization
machines · profiles · claims · the books — the shared line every tier reads, written under flywheel/
wake path · an event reaches a stopped machine and starts it
tick path · fetch → list → read → evaluate → effect, the same at every tier
a machine · dashed and grey when it is stopped between events
a repository on the git host
exactly-once responses — one keyed record per response, and a repeat under the same key writes nothing (111, 153) · git is the one state store, every write a compare-and-swap (I14, I15, 134)
one organization per pool host (241) · a secret never travels through the page — the platform's store injects it at start, and a missing one waits under attention (207, 229)

a tier is a binding, not an architecture: it changes where the tick is invoked, what the process clones and who owns the bot, and no machine, atom or profile operation (217j) · 111 · 134 · 136 · 153 · 205 · 207 · 218 · 231 · 241 · 244 · 245 · 246 · 247
per-tenant machines earn their place at tiers 2 and 3, where the tenant pays and isolation is the product; a shared batch ticker reaches the same two always-on parts with fewer, and bends only 231
